title: Role Acceptance & Early Success Commitment Agreement
body:
Purpose:
This template captures a short, mutual agreement between the hiring manager, the new hire, and People Ops to accelerate time-to-impact while keeping clear ownership and early risk signals visible. Use this document as a living artifact: it summarizes the hiring context and interview signals, sets the first 14 / 30 / 90 day commitments, and lists concrete onboarding actions and escalation paths.

Intent and scope:
- Make expectations explicit for both manager and new hire to reduce misalignment at the start.
- Document hiring evidence and outstanding risks from the interview loop.
- Provide a compact checklist for the first 14 days (fast stabilization) and clear 30/90 day success metrics.
- Capture who owns what (manager, buddy, people-ops, hiring bar assessor).

Hiring summary (to be completed before offer acceptance):
- Role: Senior Backend Engineer (Serving Runtime)
- Team: eng-serving-runtime
- Recruiter: Marcus Liu
- Interview lead: Sofia Reyes
- Expected start date: 2025-08-18
- Compensation band: L5 (range confirmed in offer)
- Primary team objectives for hire: reduce 95th-pct latency variance on streaming inference; own KV cache refactor proof-of-concept; participate in on-call rotation after 30d.

Interview evidence snapshot (summary of signals):
- Strengths observed: strong systems design, clear tradeoff reasoning on batching strategies, thoughtful debugging examples from past infra work.
- Areas flagged / development needs: limited experience with the specific runtime (GPUTch stack) and with Rust (primary infra is in Rust + C++); will need ramp on codebase idioms.
- Hiring bar assessor note: met bar for IC contribution; recommended conservative time-to-oncall (>=30d) until runtime familiarity is confirmed.

Risk triage (open items pre-hire):
- Training availability: internal Rust onboarding workshop scheduled in week 1 — need to confirm seat.
- Hardware access: dedicated dev GPU quota pending — infra to provision by day 3.
- Team bandwidth: two planned mid-Aug sprints; expected pairing allocation must be confirmed to avoid overcommittment.

Manager & People Ops commitments (what we will do):
- Manager (Sofia Reyes): assign a buddy within 48 hours; schedule 1:1 weekly for first 90 days; ensure dev GPU and codebase tour sessions booked; provide a concrete first-sprint ticket within day 2.
- Buddy (Ethan Chen): daily async check-ins week 1; pair on first PR; maintain a short knowledge map of common dev-flows.
- People Ops (Aisha Patel): confirm offer paperwork and benefits by day 0; coordinate Rust workshop seat and onboarding calendar; run 7-day new-hire pulse survey and escalate any negative signals within 48 hours.

New hire commitments (what we ask the new hire to do):
- Complete pre-start reading list (links included in onboarding tracker) by day 0.
- Complete internal Rust primer and first repo readme by day 7.
- Merge first small bugfix/visibility PR by day 14 (paired with buddy).
- Deliver a 15-minute ramp-up demo: architecture overview + 30d plan by day 30.

First 14-day stabilization checklist (concrete tasks):
Day 0 – 2:
- Complete HR paperwork and benefits orientation (People Ops).
- Meet team + buddy, set up 1:1 cadence with manager.
- Dev workstation and GPU access confirmed; SSH/keys set.
- Slack channels, calendar, monitoring dashboard access granted.

Day 3 – 7:
- Run full local dev start flow and smoke test.
- Walkthrough of serving-runtime repo: owner-led tour + README mapping.
- Attend Rust primer workshop and record any blocking questions.
- Small pairing session to debug a failing integration test.

Day 8 – 14:
- Open first PR: small bugfix or monitoring alert triage (buddy pair).
- Complete short security and incident response micro-training.
- Participate in team planning and pick the sprint ticket owner.
- 14-day pulse: manager & people-ops check-in; assess blockers and confidence level.

Managers checklist (what to track at 14 days):
- Has the new hire completed dev start and run smoke tests unassisted? (yes/no)
- Is the buddy pairing schedule being followed? (weekly minutes logged)
- Any unresolved access or infra blockers? (list & owner)
- Confidence level (manager-rated 15) on time-to-oncall readiness.

30 / 60 / 90 day milestones and success metrics:
- 30-day: merged 1 meaningful PR; presented ramp demo; passed staged infra walkthrough; buddy confirms basic codebase navigation.
- 60-day: owning one medium-sized ticket end-to-end; participating in on-call shadowing; measurable reduction in review cycle time for owned modules.
- 90-day: primary owner of a stabilization or performance workstream (e.g., KV cache module); data-backed metric improvement (latency variance reduced on owned path); full rotation into on-call.

Interview rubric summary (visible to new hire):
- System design (30%): can articulate tradeoffs, latency vs throughput, stateful streaming considerations.
- Coding (25%): correctness, testability, PR hygiene, small-system implementation.
- Debugging & incident reasoning (20%): ability to triage, isolate, and propose mitigations.
- Behavioral & collaboration (15%): ownership, communication, feedback loop.
- Domain knowledge (10%): familiarity with serving runtimes, batching, quantization fundamentals.

Escalation & remediation path (if early concerns arise):
- Day 014 red flags: manager flags concerns in 14-day check-in -> People Ops and hiring bar reviewer notified within 48 hours; defined remediation plan: extended buddy pairing, focused learning goals, scoped low-risk tickets.
- Day 1545 unresolved performance gap: role-transition conversation; possible extension of probation trial up to additional 30 days or redeployment to a role matching strengths.

Feedback & measurement cadence:
- People Ops pulse surveys: day 7, day 14, day 30.
- Manager 1:1 notes and SLO: weekly for first 90 days, then biweekly.
- Hiring bar retrospective: hiring manager writes a short note at day 30 capturing what interview signals correlated with ramp success/failure.

Checklist for closing the loop (by day 30):
- Manager submits '30-day ramp note' to hiring-archive (Confluence).
- Hiring bar assessor archives interview synthesis and updates rubric if new consistent gaps are observed.
- People Ops files a short onboarding retrospective if more than one blocker appears across hires that month.

Signatures (acknowledgement):
- New hire: _______________________  Date: ____________
- Manager: ________________________  Date: ____________
- People Ops: ______________________  Date: ____________

Notes and templates attached (links to be filled in onboarding tracker):
- Pre-start reading list (link)
notes:
This is intended as a lightweight agreement and checklist; keep it short and copy into offer playbooks when role-specific variations are needed. Avoid over-prescribing tasks that block the new hire on day 1.

Version history: 2025-07-10 created by Aisha Patel; 2025-07-22 edits from Sofia Reyes (manager expectations); 2025-08-02 minor language edits and added escalation flow.
